pages.textMedium:
Nana and Nuni were rabbits. Fluffy ones, with long ears that hung all the way down to their knees. (Do not laugh at the ears. The ears are important later.)

One evening they were watching TV. And then they saw it.

THE BIGGEST CARROT IN THE WORLD.
pages.textLong:
Nana and Nuni were rabbits. Fluffy ones, with long ears that hung all the way down to their knees. (Do not laugh at the ears. The ears are important later.)

One evening they were watching TV. And then they saw it.

THE BIGGEST CARROT IN THE WORLD.

pages.textMedium:
Now, if you know one thing about rabbits, it's this: rabbits love carrots.

Nana's mouth fell open. Nuni's nose started to twitch.

"We're getting that carrot," said Nana. "And we're bringing it home," said Nuni.

They packed two sandwiches and left before the show was even over.
pages.textLong:
Now, if you know one thing about rabbits, it's this: rabbits love carrots.

Nana's mouth fell open. Nuni's nose started to twitch.

"We're getting that carrot," said Nana. "And we're bringing it home," said Nuni.

They packed two sandwiches and left before the show was even over.

pages.textMedium:
The mysterious land was far away. And it was weird. The trees were blue. The river ran uphill. A snail overtook them. Twice.

They ate the first sandwich under a mushroom as big as an umbrella.

"The other one we save," said Nana. "For emergencies."
pages.textLong:
The mysterious land was far away. And it was weird. The trees were blue. The river ran uphill. A snail overtook them. Twice.

They ate the first sandwich under a mushroom as big as an umbrella.

"The other one we save," said Nana. "For emergencies."
pages.scene: The mysterious land, bright daytime: blue trees, curly spiral plants like the ones on the mountain, and a river that clearly flows up and over a hill. Nana and Nuni sit side by side under a spotted mushroom as big as an umbrella, sharing one sandwich, cheeks full, a little puzzled by the place. Nana holds the second sandwich safely against his chest. Lively detail: the small orange snail from the other pictures cruising past them on the path, looking smug. The two-peaked purple mountain with the tiny carrot far off on the horizon. Nana is the cream rabbit with the blue scarf and red backpack, Nuni the grey rabbit with the yellow scarf and green backpack.

pages.textLong:
On the path sat a frog. A purple frog, as big as a sofa.

"Excuse me," said Nuni. "Which way to the biggest carrot in the world?"

The frog said nothing. It just pointed with its tongue. Up. Way up. So far up that the rabbits had to lie on their backs to see the top.
pages.scene: NEW CHARACTER (needed as the strange creature of the mysterious land): a huge, calm, friendly purple frog as big as a sofa sits in the middle of the path, its long pink tongue stretched straight up like a pointing arrow. Nana and Nuni lie flat on their backs in front of it, ears spread on the ground, staring up at the purple mountain that rises out of the top of the picture into the clouds. Lively detail: the little snail riding on the frog's head. Blue trees and spiral plants around.

pages.textMedium:
The carrot grew on top of a gigantic mountain, right in the middle of the mysterious land.

So they climbed. They climbed past the trees. They climbed past the clouds. They climbed until their legs felt like spaghetti.

"Almost... there..." puffed Nuni.
pages.textLong:
The carrot grew on top of a gigantic mountain, right in the middle of the mysterious land.

So they climbed. They climbed past the trees. They climbed past the clouds. They climbed until their legs felt like spaghetti.

"Almost... there..." puffed Nuni.

It was not almost there. There was a whole lot more mountain.

On a ledge stood a goat, chewing. It looked at the rabbits. Then it looked at Nana's backpack. For a long time.

"That's the emergency sandwich," said Nana. "Don't even think about it."

The goat thought about it.
pages.scene: A narrow rock ledge high on the purple mountain, clouds below. The white mountain goat from the climbing picture stretches its neck toward Nana's red backpack, where the corner of a sandwich sticks out; its eyes are fixed on it, still chewing. Nana hugs the backpack away with both arms and gives the goat a stern look. Nuni lies flat on his back, worn out, ears spread like a starfish, tongue out. Lively detail: the little snail climbing straight up the rock wall past them.

pages.textMedium:
At last they stood on the very top. And there was the carrot! Huge! Orange! Beautiful!

...on the OTHER mountain top. Right across from them.

"You have GOT to be kidding," said Nana.

Climbing down and up again would take days.
pages.textLong:
At last they stood on the very top. And there was the carrot! Huge! Orange! Beautiful!

...on the OTHER mountain top. Right across from them.

"You have GOT to be kidding," said Nana.

Climbing down and up again would take days.

pages.textMedium:
Then Nuni looked at Nana's ears. Nana looked at Nuni's ears.

"Are you thinking what I'm thinking?"

They spun their ears. Nana's went one way each, and he just twirled on the spot like a spinning top. Nuni's tied themselves in a knot.

So. Not flying yet.
pages.textLong:
Then Nuni looked at Nana's ears. Nana looked at Nuni's ears.

"Are you thinking what I'm thinking?"

They spun their ears. Nana's went one way each, and he just twirled on the spot like a spinning top. Nuni's tied themselves in a knot.

So. Not flying yet.
pages.scene: On the first peak, the giant carrot visible on the other peak in the background. Nana whirls on one foot like a spinning top, one ear flung left and one right, eyes turned to dizzy spirals, spin lines around him. Nuni sits on the ground with his two ears tied in a big bow knot on top of his head, cross-eyed as he looks up at it. Lively detail: the blue bird from the next picture perched on a rock with one wing over its eyes. The little snail watches too.

pages.textMedium:
They untied Nuni and tried again. Round and round, faster and faster — FLAP-FLAP-FLAP-FLAP — until they lifted off the ground like two fluffy helicopters.

(Told you the ears were important.)

A bird flew past and nearly fell out of the sky.
pages.textLong:
They untied Nuni and tried again. Round and round, faster and faster — FLAP-FLAP-FLAP-FLAP — until they lifted off the ground like two fluffy helicopters.

(Told you the ears were important.)

A bird flew past and nearly fell out of the sky.

Halfway across, Nuni looked down. Never look down.

Below them was nothing. A lot of nothing, with mist in it.

His ears went slow. Flap... flap... flop. He sank into the mist until only the tips showed.

"SPIN, NUNI!" yelled Nana. "THINK OF THE CARROT!"
pages.scene: Mid-air between the two peaks, above a sea of white mist. Nana hovers with his ear rotor spinning fast, shouting downward, one paw stretched down. Below him Nuni has sunk into the mist: only his worried eyes and his two ears, slowly flopping instead of spinning, stick out. The carrot peak is close on the right. Lively detail: the blue bird flying beside Nana, pointing down at Nuni with a wing, alarmed. Funny, not frightening.

pages.textMedium:
They landed right next to the carrot. It was as big as a bus. They hugged it. They danced around it.

Then Nana stopped. "Um. Nuni? How do we get it home?"

They pushed. They pulled. The carrot did not move one tiny bit.
pages.textLong:
Nuni thought of the carrot. FLAP-FLAP-FLAP! Up he came.

They landed right next to it. It was as big as a bus. They hugged it. They danced around it.

Then Nana stopped. "Um. Nuni? How do we get it home?"

They pushed. They pulled. The carrot did not move one tiny bit.

"Fine," said Nuni. "Then we eat it right here."

They bit. They chewed. They chewed until their jaws ached. Then they stepped back to look.

Two tiny dents. That was all.

Nana counted on his paws. "At this speed we finish in four years."

They had not packed for four years.
pages.scene: The bus-sized carrot lying on the volcano peak, filling the picture. In its side are two tiny bite marks, almost invisible on the enormous orange surface. Nana and Nuni stand back from it with round stuffed cheeks and round bellies; Nana counts on his paws with a worried frown, Nuni rubs his sore jaw. Lively detail: the blue bird inspecting the two little dents up close, unimpressed. The ladybird and the snail are on the ground nearby.

pages.textLong:
Then they tried the ears. They grabbed the carrot's leaves, one each, and spun. FLAP-FLAP-FLAP-FLAP!

Up went Nana. Up went Nuni. Up went the leaves, stretching like rubber bands.

The carrot stayed exactly where it was.

So there they hung. Two helicopters, parked in mid-air.
pages.scene: The giant carrot lying heavy and unmoved on the peak. Above its leafy end, Nana and Nuni hover with their ears spinning as rotor blurs, each gripping one long green carrot leaf with both paws; the leaves are stretched tight and thin like rubber bands. Both rabbits are red in the face with effort, legs dangling. Lively detail: the ladybird sitting calmly on top of the carrot, looking up at them.

pages.textMedium:
Then the ground felt warm under their feet. They peeked over the edge.

This mountain was a volcano!

"I have an idea," said Nuni. "If we roast the carrot in the volcano, maybe it shrinks. Then we can carry it."

It was a strange idea. But it was the only one they had.
pages.textLong:
When they dropped back down, the ground felt warm under their feet. They peeked over the edge.

This mountain was a volcano!

"I have an idea," said Nuni. "If we roast the carrot in the volcano, maybe it shrinks. Then we can carry it."

It was a strange idea. But it was the only one they had.

pages.textMedium:
So they dragged the carrot toward the crater. They heaved. They grunted. Nuni's ears went pink.

After one whole hour it had moved as far as a ladybird is long. A snail went past and did not even look.

They flopped down flat. Two tough rabbits. No muscles left.

Then somebody coughed.
pages.textLong:
So they dragged the carrot toward the crater. They heaved. They grunted. Nuni's ears went pink.

After one whole hour it had moved as far as a ladybird is long. A snail went past and did not even look.

They flopped down flat. Two tough rabbits. No muscles left.

Then somebody coughed.
pages.scene: The volcano peak, the giant carrot with a rope tied around its leafy end, the glowing crater a long way off on the left. Nana and Nuni have flopped flat on the ground beside the rope, arms and ears spread, tongues out, completely worn out. Behind the carrot there is a tiny drag mark in the dust, exactly as long as the ladybird standing next to it. The snail glides past, nose in the air. Lively detail: a big horse-shaped shadow with two pointed ears falls across the rabbits from outside the picture.

pages.textMedium:
"Need a hand? Or a hoof?"

Behind them stood a horse. A big, friendly horse who had ALSO seen the carrot on TV, and had ALSO climbed all the way up here.

"Help us push," said Nana, "and we share."

"Deal," said the horse.
pages.textLong:
"Need a hand? Or a hoof?"

Behind them stood a horse. A big, friendly horse who had ALSO seen the carrot on TV, and had ALSO climbed all the way up here.

"Help us push," said Nana, "and we share."

"Deal," said the horse.

The horse had no helicopter ears. So he had done it the slow way. Down the first mountain, up the second. It took four days.

On day two he had eaten his map.

"You flew across?" said the horse. "In about a minute?"

"Sort of," said Nuni.

The horse had to sit down.
pages.scene: The brown horse with the white blaze and the small purple saddle bag sits down heavily on his haunches beside the giant carrot, jaw hanging open, stunned. In front of him Nuni whirls one ear like a little propeller to show how it works, a bit embarrassed, while Nana points back across the misty gap to the first peak. Lively detail: a half-chewed corner of a map sticking out of the horse's purple bag. His hooves are dusty from the long walk.

pages.textMedium:
With a horse, the carrot moved. They heaved it to the edge. One, two, three — PUSH! It rolled over and dropped into the volcano.

Then they sat down and waited. They shared the emergency sandwich three ways. The horse counted to a hundred. Twice.

Nothing happened. Nothing at all.
pages.textLong:
With a horse, the carrot moved. They heaved it to the edge. One, two, three — PUSH! It rolled over and dropped into the volcano.

Then they sat down and waited. They shared the emergency sandwich three ways. The horse counted to a hundred. Twice.

Nothing happened. Nothing at all.
pages.scene: The crater rim seen from the side: Nana, Nuni and the horse sit in a row on the edge with their legs and hooves dangling over, faces lit orange from below, staring down into the glow where the carrot has gone. Each holds one third of a sandwich; the horse's piece looks tiny in his hoof. They look bored and hopeful at once. Lively detail: the ladybird sits at the end of the row with one crumb of its own. A thin wisp of smoke rises from the crater.

pages.textMedium:
Then the ladybird started to run. That is never a good sign.

Rumble. Grumble. BRRRUMBLE. The ground shook. Little stones hopped about like popcorn. The two rabbits and the horse grabbed each other and screamed.

"AAAAAAH!" "EEEEEEK!" "NEEEEEIGH!"
pages.textLong:
Then the ladybird started to run. That is never a good sign.

Rumble. Grumble. BRRRUMBLE. The ground shook. Little stones hopped about like popcorn. The two rabbits and the horse grabbed each other and screamed.

"AAAAAAH!" "EEEEEEK!" "NEEEEEIGH!"

pages.textMedium:
WHOOOOSH! The carrot shot out of the volcano like a rocket, trailing smoke and sparks.

It flew over the mountains, over the clouds, over the whole mysterious land — and landed, THUNK, right outside Nana and Nuni's front door.

Not smaller. Just nicely roasted.
pages.textLong:
WHOOOOSH! The carrot shot out of the volcano like a rocket, trailing smoke and sparks.

It flew over the mountains, over the clouds, over the whole mysterious land — and landed, THUNK, right outside Nana and Nuni's front door.

Not smaller. Just nicely roasted.

pages.textMedium:
Now they had to catch up with their dinner.

Nana and Nuni spun their ears. The horse held on to their feet. FLAP-FLAP-FLAP... They got off the ground. Barely.

They flew so low that the horse's hooves combed every treetop in the mysterious land.

"Higher!" said the horse.

"This IS higher!" puffed Nana.
pages.textLong:

pages.scene: Flying home over the mysterious land in warm evening light. Nana and Nuni fly side by side with their ears spinning as rotor blurs, both straining, cheeks puffed. The big brown horse hangs underneath, holding one rabbit foot in each front hoof, eyes wide, his back hooves dragging through the tops of the blue trees and knocking leaves loose. Far ahead in the sky, the thin smoke trail of the carrot leads toward home. Lively detail: down on the path the sofa-sized purple frog waves goodbye with its tongue, the snail on its head.

pages.textMedium:
They came down with a bump, right by their own front door. The horse came down first. The snail was already there. (Nobody knows how.)

That night they ate roasted carrot until they couldn't move, and there was still enough left for a hundred breakfasts.

Then all three fell asleep in a heap. Because even the toughest rabbits in the world have to sleep sometime.
